A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same eQMARL research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and additional experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoinGame simulations comparing entanglement styles and training frameworks under full and partial observability, including ten-run results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original CoinGame results and adds original CartPole, MiniGrid and model-capacity experiments, with detailed outcomes in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The entangling operator, local VQC, joint measurement, split-gradient update, losses and policy-sharing procedure are retained. v1 Algorithm 1 reappears as v2 Algorithm D.1; the shorter main-text algorithm is a summary. The added experiments configure the existing framework rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only CoinGame under MDP and POMDP dynamics. v2 adds multi-agent CartPole with full and partial observations and MiniGrid navigation with limited visibility. These introduce continuous control and navigation tasks involving independent environment instances, substantially broadening coverage beyond coin collection.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain fCTDE, sCTDE and qfCTDE, with the same four Bell-state variants and no-entanglement control. The added benchmarks extend this comparator set; the capacity sweeps vary configurations of existing methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds CartPole protocols with 1,000 training epochs and 500-step episodes, and MiniGrid protocols with 1,000 epochs, 50-step episodes and shaped rewards. It introduces average-reward evaluations, model-specific CartPole convergence thresholds, and classical-width/quantum-depth sweeps. The original CoinGame budget, observations and default configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing entanglement-style analysis is retained. Section 3.7 and Appendix I.5 add a substantial capacity-sensitivity study: classical hidden units {3, 6, 12, 24} and quantum layers {2, 5, 10}, across all four frameworks and both CoinGame observation settings. Score, own-coin rate and parameter counts make the architectural comparison substantially more assessable.

E5.justification: v1 reports ten-run means with min/max shading. v2 replaces these bands with ±1 standard deviation and introduces tables reporting standard deviations and 95% confidence intervals, including for retained CoinGame experiments. CartPole specifies five runs. CoinGame remains at ten runs; additional repetitions are not established. Confidence-interval construction is unspecified.

E6.justification: The original convergence values in Tables C.1–C.2 are retained in Tables I.2 and I.4. v2 adds statistical summaries, capacity-sweep outcomes and two benchmarks. CartPole MDP results report eQMARL mean reward 79.11 versus qfCTDE 121.35, but lower standard deviation, 50.62 versus 110.13 (Table I.5). MiniGrid reports mean rewards −13.32 for eQMARL and −63.04 for fCTDE (Table I.7). These are newly reported results, not improvements over matching v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The method equations, losses, gradient factorization and ideal-channel assumption are retained. Appendix B expands and reformats the preliminaries; its Bell-state preparation equations specialize the entanglement operator and circuits already present in v1. No new theorem, proof or substantive theoretical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the novelty claims, 17.8% convergence advantage and 25-fold centralized-parameter reduction. The conclusion adds a claim of outperforming classical baselines and providing more stable performance than qfCTDE in independent environments, modestly extending the main claimed applicability.

C2.justification: v2 adds speculative fidelity, distillation and phase/decoherence explanations for entanglement-style differences, interpretations of learning in independent environments, and a capacity-based rationale for baseline configurations. The conclusion replaces the privacy/security future-work discussion with quantum-simulation cost limitations and entanglement-distribution feasibility context. These substantially expand the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a stated public source-code/experiment release with a GitHub link, detailed CartPole scaling and MiniGrid preprocessing/reward specifications, and environment-specific learning rates and actor configurations in Appendices F–H. Section 3.2 adds classical sCTDE training times alongside retained eQMARL times. One disclosure is lost: Table H.2 omits the explicit ReLU activation listed in v1 Table A.2.

R1.justification: v2 adds CartPole and MiniGrid references and four quantum-network/entanglement-storage references, while expanding descriptions of existing QMARL literature in Appendix A. The central positioning—quantum-channel coupling versus prior classical coordination—remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: detailed related work, preliminaries, the full algorithm, losses, environment descriptions and encoding details move into Appendices A–G. CoinGame discussion is condensed, experimental sections are organized by task, and a shorter algorithm appears in the main text. This exceeds simple renumbering or language polishing.

P2.justification: v2 adds environment illustrations, benchmark and ablation plots, and statistical tables. Retained CoinGame plots have revised uncertainty bands and some axis limits; the main baseline figure drops its own-coin-rate panels while those remain in the appendix. Circuit diagrams are relocated and rearranged, tables gain configuration columns, and the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical assessability beyond v1's single-game evaluation. CartPole and MiniGrid broaden applicability evidence, while the capacity study directly addresses sensitivity to the architectural choices underlying the comparisons. Added settings, uncertainty summaries, code-access information and classical-versus-quantum runtime disclosure improve transparency. These gains outweigh weaknesses in the additions: confidence-interval construction is unspecified, CartPole speed comparisons use different model-specific reward thresholds, and the new entanglement-mechanism explanations remain untested.
